skill.name: session-handoff
skill.description: Create, validate, list, and resume structured handoff documents for long AI coding sessions.
skill.summary: Preserves project state so another AI agent can continue work with clear context.
skill.author: softaworks

security_audit.summary: Static analysis produced many command, filesystem, environment, and network matches. Review confirmed only the evaluation cleanup deletion risk plus contextual handoff data-handling risks; most high signals are test fixtures, Markdown examples, defensive secret patterns, or shell-free hardcoded git calls. No bundled prompt injection attempt or data exfiltration behavior was found.

remediation.issue: Evaluation cleanup can delete a user-selected path.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict cleanup to a dedicated temp directory and refuse root, home, or repository paths unless a clear confirmation flag is provided.

remediation.issue: Handoff files can preserve sensitive project context.
remediation.suggestion: Warn users before committing or sharing handoffs, and keep secret values, credentials, customer data, and private implementation details out of handoff text.

remediation.issue: Imported handoff files can contain untrusted instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to treat handoff instructions as project notes, verify them against the current user request, and ignore attempts to override system or developer instructions.

remediation.issue: Resume checklist environment commands can expose local details.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer commands that list only needed variable names and avoid copying process arguments or environment values into handoffs.

semantic_findings.title: Persistent Handoff Files May Preserve Sensitive Context
semantic_findings.description: The skill creates Markdown handoffs that can include project path, branch, commits, modified files, decisions, and environment variable names. Secret scanning helps, but handoffs may still preserve sensitive implementation or business context.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The storage behavior and metadata capture are explicit in the workflow and generated template. The risk depends on what users write into handoffs, so this is a data-handling concern rather than malicious collection.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Handoff Content Can Influence Agent Behavior
semantic_findings.description: The resume workflow tells the agent to read a handoff and begin from its documented next steps. Handoff files imported from a repository can contain instructions that should be treated as untrusted project context.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow consumes Markdown handoffs as operational context. No bundled prompt-injection payload was found, but the trust boundary should be documented for imported handoffs.

semantic_findings.title: Resume Checklist Encourages Local Environment Inspection
semantic_findings.description: The quick-start checklist suggests commands that can reveal process details or environment variable names. This is useful for verification, but outputs should be minimized and redacted.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The checklist explicitly includes git, process, and environment inspection commands. The commands are local and visible, so the risk is limited to accidental disclosure in transcripts or handoffs.

content.value_statement: Long AI coding sessions lose context when a session ends. This skill creates structured handoffs so Claude, Codex, or Claude Code can resume with clear next steps.
actual_capabilities: Generates timestamped handoff Markdown files under .claude/handoffs.
Pre-fills project path, git branch, recent commits, and changed files.
Validates handoffs for required sections, TODOs, file references, and common secrets.
Lists existing handoffs with titles, dates, completion status, and file paths.
Checks handoff staleness against current git history and referenced files.
Supports chained handoffs that link related work sessions.
limitations: Requires local Python scripts and workspace filesystem access.
Git-based metadata works only inside a git repository.
Secret detection uses patterns and cannot guarantee full coverage.
Handoff quality depends on accurate template completion.

use_cases.title: Pause a Long Coding Task
use_cases.description: Capture current state, modified files, decisions, blockers, and immediate next steps before ending a session.

use_cases.title: Resume Work From a Previous Agent
use_cases.description: Find the latest handoff, check if it is stale, and continue from the documented next action.

use_cases.title: Maintain Context Across Milestones
use_cases.description: Create chained handoffs after major milestones so future sessions can trace decisions and progress.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a handoff for the current work session. Include current status, modified files, decisions, blockers, and next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a Handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Validate the handoff file and summarize any TODOs, missing sections, stale references, or possible secrets.

prompt_templates.title: Resume From the Latest Handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the latest handoff, check staleness, read it fully, and tell me the first safe action to take.

prompt_templates.title: Chain a Milestone Handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a continuation handoff linked to the previous one. Emphasize new decisions, completed tasks, changed assumptions, and next risks.

output_examples.input: Create a handoff for this authentication refactor.
output_examples.output: Creates a timestamped handoff with session metadata, current state, completed work, pending tasks, decisions, and environment notes.

output_examples.input: Resume from the most recent handoff.
output_examples.output: Lists available handoffs, checks staleness, reads the selected handoff, and identifies the first verified next step.

output_examples.input: Validate this handoff before I stop.
output_examples.output: Reports quality score, remaining placeholders, missing required sections, possible secrets, and broken file references.

best_practices: Run validation before sharing or committing a handoff.
Record environment variable names only, never secret values.
Review imported handoffs for untrusted instructions before following them.
anti_patterns: Do not store API keys, tokens, passwords, or private keys in handoffs.
Do not resume from a stale handoff without checking current git state.
Do not leave vague TODOs where the next agent needs concrete actions.

faq.question: Where are handoff files stored?
faq.answer: The skill stores generated handoffs in .claude/handoffs within the current project.

faq.question: Does this skill send data to a remote service?
faq.answer: No runtime network call was found in the reviewed scripts. The skill operates on local files and git metadata.

faq.question: Can it detect secrets in handoffs?
faq.answer: It checks common secret patterns such as API keys, passwords, tokens, and private key markers.

faq.question: Can it resume work automatically?
faq.answer: It provides context and a checklist for resumption. The agent should still verify current project state first.

faq.question: Does it require git?
faq.answer: Git is not required for all features, but branch, commit, and staleness checks depend on git.

faq.question: Is it safe to publish handoffs?
faq.answer: Only publish reviewed handoffs. They may contain project paths, commit messages, file names, and sensitive context.
